data.cultural_impact: Avula is a name deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and culture. It is primarily known as the alternate name for the goddess Durga, who is revered as the warrior goddess and the protective mother figure in Hinduism. Avula further signifies the strength and power embodied by Durga. In Hindu tradition, Avulomba or Avula Puja is performed to appease the goddess and seek her blessings for prosperity, protection, and well-being.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Avula holds immense spiritual significance. As an alternate name for Durga, it represents the formidable, unconquerable nature of the goddess. Avula signifies the spiritual power of protection, strength, and compassion. In Hinduism, the quest for spiritual growth and self-realization can be facilitated through the invocation and connection with the goddess Avula/Durga. Her blessings are believed to help individuals on their spiritual journey to achieve inner peace, mental balance, and overall well-being.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Avula is a Sanskrit name meaning 'One who purifies'. It symbolizes the inner journey towards spiritual cleansing and self-realization. The name is a reminder to constantly strive for purity in thoughts, words, and actions, and to maintain a clear and focused mind on the path to enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Avula Ramalinga Reddy was a ruler of the Avulapura (Avulapadi) kingdom in Andhra Pradesh, India, during the late 16th and early 17th centuries. He was a vassal of the Vijayanagara Empire, and his kingdom was located in what is now the Guntur district.

Avula Mahadeva was a Jaina monk who lived around the 12th century in India. He is known for his contributions to Jaina literature, particularly his work on the Tattvartha Sutra, a canonical text in the Digambara tradition of Jainism.
historical_references.context: Jaina monk, Contributions to Jaina literature
